title: Incident notification timeline and customer communication scripts
content:
Purpose:
This working draft defines a pragmatic notification timeline and a set of reusable customer-facing communication scripts for security incidents that may affect Redwood Inference customers (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). The goal is to balance legal/regulatory obligations, customer trust, and operational clarity: give customers timely, factual, and actionable information while preserving an effective internal response.

Scope:
- Applies to incidents that materially impact confidentiality, integrity, or availability of customer data or model inference (data exfiltration, unauthorized access to call data, persistent outage, or severe degradation).
- Covers communication to customers, account teams, and public notice where required.
- Does NOT replace internal incident handling checklists (triage, forensics, mitigation). This complements the IR technical runbook.

High-level timing principles (applicable unless otherwise directed by Legal):
- Immediate internal alert: within 15 minutes of detection to on-call SRE/IR hotline.
- Initial customer acknowledgement: within 4 hours for incidents likely to affect customers; within 24 hours for lower-likelihood/no-impact events.
- Regulatory-required notification: follow applicable laws (e.g., GDPR 72-hour assessment). If a personal data breach under GDPR is likely, prepare regulators within 72 hours of becoming aware; proceed with customer notice concurrently.
- Substantive update cadence: first substantive update within 24 hours of initial notice; then every 24–48 hours while the incident is active or until the situation has stabilized.
- Final report: within 30 days of detection where feasible, longer if forensic work requires.

Severity definitions (for communications):
- P0 (Critical security incident): confirmed unauthorized access to production customer data, confirmed exfiltration, or compromise of encryption/key management. Requires immediate escalation and direct customer outreach.
- P1 (Major incident): sustained outage affecting production inference for multiple customers or confirmed unauthorized access to non-sensitive customer metadata. High-priority customer notification.
- P2 (Partial impact): transient outages, degraded performance, or limited-scope exposure with low risk. Targeted notifications for affected customers.
- P3 (Low / informational): internal detections unlikely to affect customers; optional customer notification only if material change to customer risk is identified.

Required elements for any customer notice (minimal checklist):
- Incident ID (IR-YYYYMMDD-####)
- Summary: brief, non-technical summary of what happened and what was affected
- Severity classification (P0–P3) and why
- Services/regions/customers affected (list or "no customer data impacted")
- Technical summary (concise): what systems, what type of data, and how it occurred (if known)
- Mitigation steps taken and status (contained, ongoing, resolved)
- Recommended customer actions (credential rotation, audit logs review, etc.)
- Contact/escrow support path (AM, security@redwood.ai, dedicated incident channel)
- Links to live status/incident page and follow-up report ETA

Communication templates
(Insert the placeholders: {customer_name}, {incident_id}, {service_list}, {affected_regions}, {technical_summary}, {mitigation_status}, {next_update_eta}, {account_manager}, {support_link})

1) P0 — Immediate direct customer outreach (email + phone script)
Subject: [Urgent] Incident {incident_id}: Immediate notice for {service_list}
Email body:
Hi {customer_name},

We are contacting you about an active security incident (ID {incident_id}) affecting {service_list}. At this time we have confirmed unauthorized access to customer inference logs/weights (or insert specific scope). We are treating this as a P0 incident.

What we know now:
- Affected services/regions: {affected_regions}
- Short technical summary: {technical_summary}
- Current status: {mitigation_status} (containment is in progress / fully contained)

What we are doing:
- Our incident response team and external forensics partner are engaged and actively investigating.
- We have isolated the affected infrastructure and revoked the compromised credentials/keys where relevant.
- Rolling mitigations (patch, config changes, rekeying) are in process.

Recommended customer actions:
- Immediately rotate any API keys/credentials that may have been used with the affected services.
- Review your logs for unusual activity related to the dates/times in the technical summary.

We will provide a substantive update by {next_update_eta}. Your account manager {account_manager} is available for direct coordination. For urgent security questions, contact security@redwood.ai or use your assigned incident channel.

We understand the severity of this and apologize for the disruption.

Phone/VM script (short):
"Hi {customer_contact}, this is {account_manager} from Redwood Inference. I want to make you aware of incident {incident_id} that may affect {service_list}. We’ve classified this as P0. We’ve sent an email with full details — are you on a secure line to discuss now?"

2) P1 — High-priority email (single-channel)
Subject: Incident {incident_id}: Service impact to {service_list}
Body:
Hello {customer_name},

We are investigating incident {incident_id} impacting {service_list} in {affected_regions}. We have observed [describe outage or access]. At this stage, we believe the impact is limited to [scope].

Mitigation and next steps:
- Actions taken: {mitigation_status}
- Next update: {next_update_eta}

If you experience service disruption, contact {account_manager} or support at {support_link}.

3) P2 — Targeted notice for affected customers
Subject: Notice: {service_list} incident {incident_id} — limited impact
Body:
Hi {customer_name},

We detected an issue (ID {incident_id}) that caused degraded performance for {service_list}. No evidence of data exfiltration at this time. We have applied the fix and are monitoring.

Actions for customers: none required / recommended action: brief list.

4) P3 — Optional informational bulletin
Subject: Informational: internal security event {incident_id}
Body:
Short note summarizing detection and confirmation of no customer impact. No action required.

Public-facing notice template (for major incidents only — coordinate with Legal & Comms):
Headline: Redwood Inference incident {incident_id} — service disruption and customer impact
Lead paragraph: A security incident affecting {service_list} was detected on {date}. We launched our incident response plan, engaged third-party forensics, and are actively remediating.
Key facts (bullet list):
- Incident ID: {incident_id}
- Date/time first detected: {first_detected}
- Services impacted: {service_list}
- Customer impact: {summary_of_customer_impact}
- Mitigation status: {mitigation_status}
Call to action: contact security@redwood.ai for affected customers; visit {status_page} for updates.

Escalation & internal routing (quick reference):
- Detection -> on-call SRE & IR lead within 15 minutes
- IR lead -> Security Head & General Counsel if P0/P1 within 1 hour
- P0 -> engage Communications, Account Execs, Legal, and external forensics within 2 hours
- Notify Sales/CS to prepare 1:1 outreach for high-value customers within 4 hours

Account team playbook (for use by AM/CS when reaching out):
- Read the official IR email exactly as sent (do not speculate).
- Offer a scheduled call within 6 hours for customers with sensitive workloads.
- Log customer-specific concerns in JIRA/CS ticket and escalate to Security if additional access logs are requested.

Legal/regulatory notes (summary):
- GDPR: assess whether the incident qualifies as a personal data breach and prepare regulator notification within 72 hours if likely. Customer notification should not be delayed pending regulator coordination.
- Contractual DPAs: review customer DPA clauses for specific timing or notification obligations (e.g., certain enterprise customers may require immediate escalation to named security contacts).
- Evidence preservation: Legal will advise on preservation and scope before any customer-provided forensic materials are shared externally.

Post-incident follow-up items (report template items):
- Chronology of events with timestamps
- Root cause analysis (RCA) and technical details
- Evidence of containment and eradication
- Customer impact assessment (who, what, when)
- Remediation actions and timelines
- Preventive controls and timeline for implementation

Appendix — Quick checklist for the notice writer:
- Confirm incident ID and severity with IR lead
- Verify affected customer list and regional scope with SRE
- Coordinate mandatory legal/regulatory phrases with Legal (e.g., "We are notifying you in accordance with applicable data protection laws")
- Avoid speculative language; limit to confirmed facts and what customers should do
- Include clear contact points and next update ETA

Notes & open questions (for working doc):
- Determine default cadence for large enterprise customers that require daily briefings vs standard 24–48 hour cadence.
- Establish a dedicated incident notification template set for Dedicated and Private customers with instructions for on-prem remediation coordination.
- Consider automating first-touch notifications through the Console and Account Manager integrations (routing rules, templated personalized messages).

This document is a living draft. Please comment inline or add issues to JIRA-SEC-278 for follow-up requirements and legal phrasing changes.

End of document."
